name: Lord Howe Island Group
blurb: Seabirds, a flightless rail and the world's southernmost coral reef.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Light drives the island forest, the algae and the reef corals alike.
Rain on the mountains feeds the forest of the island, which is wetter on its high southern peaks.
Reef-building corals form the most southerly true coral reef in the world, in a lagoon on the western side of the island.

nodes.name: Surgeonfishes
nodes.desc: Reef fishes that mostly graze algae from rock and coral, keeping the reef surface cropped.
A reef shark that eats mainly bottom-dwelling bony fishes and octopuses. Numbers rose in the marine park sanctuary zones.

story: Lord Howe Island is an irregularly crescent-shaped volcanic remnant in the Tasman Sea, part of New South Wales, Australia. The island is about 10 km long with an area of 14.55 square kilometers and is home to forested hills rising to Mount Gower. The Lord Howe Island Group comprises 28 islands, islets, and rocks, including Ball's Pyramid.
matters: The Lord Howe Island Group is a World Heritage Site with untouched forest and the world's southernmost barrier coral reef. It shelters unique plants and animals found nowhere else in the world, including the endangered and flightless Lord Howe woodhen.
